title: bug: a claim_next_task call with no workerId (a peek) still stamps the offered row's metrics.firstClaimAt and posts the #workers file-collision notice, so a terminal or tool peek skews wall-clock metrics and pages busy seats for a claim nobody made
description:
Held item from hunt #11 (task-afe61cc0, architect-74d9e1c7, msg-7ed73235), filed by the governor. Re-checked at tip 8ca8d389: claimNextTask.ts is unchanged since the repro HEAD 31492ac5. It is low and rare: the proxy injects workerId for agent seats, so only direct callers such as moe-call.sh peek.

PROBLEM. claim_next_task without a workerId assigns nothing, but it still writes. It stamps `metrics.firstClaimAt` on the offered row, and list_metrics wall-clock then starts at the peek. When the row's files overlap a peer, it also posts the #workers collision heads-up.

EVIDENCE (at 8ca8d389):
- claimNextTask.ts:860-865: `if (!task.metrics?.firstClaimAt) { … state.updateTask(task.id, { metrics: nextMetrics }, undefined, params.workerId) }` runs with no workerId guard.
- claimNextTask.ts:887-898: `state.postToRoleChannel('workers', collisionNotice(task.id, fileCollision, params.workerId))` runs with no workerId guard.
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-afe61cc0/A/zzHuntA_peekClaimWrites.test.ts with its .output.txt. "writes nothing when no worker is named" fails, "Tests 1 failed (1)".

FIX DIRECTION. Skip both writes when no workerId is supplied. Keep the offered-row response unchanged.

PLACEMENT. Open row task-4fbd3c69 may touch claimNextTask.ts around :534-544, its ATTEMPT_FINALIZING check, if it extracts a shared helper. Keep this edit inside the firstClaimAt and collision-notice blocks, add no dependsOn, and use the seat's own editor.
definitionOfDone: A claim_next_task call with no workerId leaves the offered row's metrics.firstClaimAt untouched and posts nothing to #workers, and it still returns the same offered row as before.

A claim with a workerId still stamps firstClaimAt once and still posts the collision notice exactly as before. The ported hunt repro passes, and the existing claim_next_task test files stay green in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.note: Created peek test file as specified.

implementationPlan.description:
The fix in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/claimNextTask.ts, with your Edit tool. Touch only the firstClaimAt block and the collision-post block, about :855-898. Open row task-4fbd3c69 may touch the ATTEMPT_FINALIZING area near :534-544, so stay out of it.
(a) The firstClaimAt guard becomes `if (params.workerId && !task.metrics?.firstClaimAt) {`. Append to its comment: "A peek (no workerId) claimed nothing, so it stamps nothing: wall-clock starts at the real claim."
(b) The collision post: directly above `if (fileCollision.length > 0) {`, add `// A peek still reports fileCollision in its answer, but pages nobody.` and make the condition `if (params.workerId && fileCollision.length > 0) {`.
Keep the `fileCollision` computation unconditional: the answer's `...(fileCollision.length > 0 ? { fileCollision } : {})` (about :986) must stay the same for a peek. The truthiness test matches the claim path's own `if (params.workerId)` assignment branch (about :707) and the #general 'claimed task' post, so 'a claim that assigned nothing writes nothing' holds for '' too.
Error handling: no new failure path. Both blocks keep their existing best-effort try/catch, so a stamp or post failure never blocks the claim. The guard only skips writes, it never throws, and the offered-row response is built exactly as before.
implementationPlan.note: Guarded firstClaimAt stamp and collision post with params.workerId.

(1) Scope: claimNextTask.ts changes only the two conditions and their comments, and the new test file is the only other change.
(2) Does a real claim still do everything?
- An agent seat always has a workerId, because the proxy injects MOE_WORKER_ID. So seats see no change.

(3) Could a peek now hide a real collision? No: the peek's answer still lists fileCollision. Only the page is skipped, and a page was never owed for a claim nobody made.
(4) The metrics consumers (list_metrics wall-clock) now start at the first real claim. A row first peeked and later claimed is stamped by the claim.
(5) Concurrency: no new state. The guard reads only the call's own arguments inside the existing mutex.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Three fixes were weighed.
(1) Chosen: guard the two writes with the call's workerId, as the row's fix direction says, and keep the collision computation so a peek's answer is unchanged.
(2) Rejected: skipping computeFileCollisions for peeks. That changes the offered answer (fileCollision disappears), which DoD 1 forbids.
(3) Rejected: returning early for a peek before the metrics/collision section. That would also drop the fileCollision answer and the channel ids that are built later.
The workerId truthiness test matches the existing assignment branch (`if (params.workerId)` about :707) and the #general claimed-task post, so the three post-claim writes share one predicate.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Hunt repro output: the peek published exactly two events, TASK_UPDATED (the firstClaimAt stamp) and MESSAGE_CREATED (the collision notice). Every other write in the claim path is already behind `if (params.workerId)`.
The answer's fileCollision is built from the same scan (about :986), so the scan must stay unconditional.
